summary: Noise gate and downward expander, the successor of Pedal Gate: a threshold with a separate, lower close threshold (hysteresis), attack, hold and release (linear gain ramps, as Pedal Gate's), a Range floor, an expansion ratio (infinity is a hard gate, lower ratios expand downwards), Peak or RMS detection, a key filter (low and high cut), an external sidechain on input 2, lookahead and Listen to the key. Delta (hear only what the gate takes out) and a gain-match reading. Use it to clean spill from drum tracks, tighten a bass or cut the noise between phrases.
use_for: Clean up noise, bleed and tails with a gate or downward expander, optionally keyed from a sidechain.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: The level that opens the gate
parameters.how: Sets the level in dB, from -80 to 0, at which the gate opens.
parameters.sound: Raising it silences more of the quiet noise and bleed, but cuts into soft notes if set too high.

parameters.name: Hysteresis
parameters.description: The gate closes this far under the threshold: more means less chatter
parameters.how: Makes the gate close this far below the opening level, from 0 to 20 dB.
parameters.sound: More hysteresis stops the gate chattering on and off around the threshold.

parameters.name: Ratio
parameters.description: Expansion below the close threshold: every dB under it is (ratio − 1) dB quieter, down to Range. Infinity: a hard gate that goes straight to Range
parameters.how: Sets how strongly the signal below the threshold is turned down, from 1:1 up to infinity.
parameters.sound: Low ratios fade quiet sounds gently; infinity shuts the gate completely down to the Range.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: The closed gate's gain floor: -90 dB nearly shut, 0 dB no gating
parameters.how: Sets how far a closed gate turns the signal down, from 0 to -90 dB.
parameters.sound: -90 dB gives silence between hits; a smaller range leaves some of the background, for a more natural result.

parameters.name: Attack
parameters.description: Time for the gain to open fully (a linear ramp)
parameters.how: Sets how long the gate takes to open fully, from 0.1 ms to 0.5 s.
parameters.sound: Fast attacks keep the start of a hit sharp; slow ones fade it in softly.

parameters.name: Hold
parameters.description: How long the gate stays open after the signal falls under the close threshold
parameters.how: Sets how long the gate stays open after the signal drops under the closing level, from 1 ms to 2 s.
parameters.sound: Longer holds stop the gate cutting off the ends of notes and flickering between hits.

parameters.name: Release
parameters.description: Time for the gain to close fully (a linear ramp)
parameters.how: Sets how long the gate takes to close, from 1 ms to 2 s.
parameters.sound: Short releases chop tails tightly; long ones let sounds fade out naturally.

parameters.name: Lookahead
parameters.description: Delays the audio so the gate opens before the transient arrives (latency)
parameters.how: Delays the audio by up to 25 ms so the gate opens before the transient arrives.
parameters.sound: Hits keep their sharp attack instead of being clipped at the start, at the cost of some latency.

parameters.name: Detection
parameters.description: Peak: fast, follows transients. RMS: 10 ms average, smoother on sustained sources
parameters.how: Chooses whether the gate reacts to the peak level or to a 10 ms RMS average.
parameters.sound: Peak responds instantly to hits; RMS is smoother and avoids false triggers on sustained sounds.

parameters.name: Sidechain
parameters.description: Detect from the input, or from input 2 (connect a machine to the second input)
parameters.how: Chooses whether the gate listens to its own input or to the machine on the second input.
parameters.sound: External lets another sound, such as a kick, open the gate for rhythmic chopping.

parameters.name: Key low cut
parameters.description: High-pass on the key: keeps low rumble from opening the gate (off at its minimum)
parameters.how: Filters low frequencies, from 10 Hz to 2 kHz, out of the signal the gate listens to.
parameters.sound: Rumble and bass bleed stop opening the gate, so it reacts only to the sound you want.

parameters.name: Key high cut
parameters.description: Low-pass on the key: keeps hiss and cymbals from opening the gate (off at its maximum)
parameters.how: Filters high frequencies, from 1 kHz to 22 kHz, out of the signal the gate listens to.
parameters.sound: Hiss and cymbal bleed stop opening the gate, so it reacts only to the main source.

parameters.name: Listen
parameters.how: Switches the output to the filtered key signal that the gate hears.
parameters.sound: You hear what the gate hears, which helps you set the key filters and threshold.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the gate, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)
parameters.how: Adds -24 to +24 dB of gain after the gate.
parameters.sound: It makes the gated sound louder or quieter without changing how the gate works.

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what the gate takes out: the output minus the input, delayed to match (glides over 10 ms)
parameters.how: Plays only the difference between the output and the input.
parameters.sound: You hear exactly what the gate cuts out, so you can check it leaves the wanted sound alone.

readings.description: The gate's gain now, dB (0 open, down to Range when closed)
1 while the gate is open, 0 while it is closed or closing
The lookahead, reported to NeoBuzz Live
